canonical_name: Linear programming (problem family; exact proposition open)

statement_blocker: The repository gloss names an optimization problem family, not a proposition. It fixes no decision carrier, scalar, objective orientation or coefficients, constraints or standard form, feasibility and boundedness hypotheses, optimum convention, exact conclusion, witness, or degenerate cases. Selecting attainment, an extreme-point theorem, an infeasible/unbounded/optimal alternative, duality, or algorithm correctness would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: a selected source must fix finite- or infinite-dimensional decision and constraint carriers, scalar or coefficient domain, objective/value codomain, index types, universes, matrix or linear-map representation, and all algebraic, order, topological, and finiteness instances.
conclusion: Open at intake. The catalog does not distinguish construction of an LP, existence or attainment, an extreme/basic-feasible optimizer, an infeasible/unbounded/optimal alternative, weak or strong duality, a certificate theorem, or algorithm correctness.
degenerate_case_status: Nothing is silently excluded before statement selection; zero-dimensional data, absent or redundant constraints, empty or infeasible feasible sets, zero or unbounded objectives, rank deficiency, nonattainment, multiple optima, and infinite values require explicit source-faithful treatment.
candidate_scope_not_credited: existence or attainment of an optimum for a source-specified bounded or compact feasible polyhedron
the fundamental theorem that an attained optimum may be realized at an extreme point or basic feasible solution
an exact infeasible, unbounded, or optimal alternative with certificates
weak or strong primal-dual linear-programming duality and complementary slackness
correctness, termination, or complexity of a specified LP algorithm
excluded_substitutions: Farkas' lemma, conic duality, or polyhedral geometry selected without an approved source-identity bridge
one-dimensional, unconstrained, feasibility-only, or bounded special cases
generic convexity, separation, order, matrix, or linear-map APIs treated as the root
the meta linarith simplex oracle treated as a kernel theorem or target proof
an assumed LP result, opaque predicate, certificate field, or existential projected directly from a hypothesis
the catalog label 已验证 or the API probe treated as source or proof evidence
